_readme: This file is SAMPLE data. Keys must be the hospital's exact OpenStreetMap 'name' tag, lowercased, on the specific OSM element tagged amenity=hospital (large hospital campuses are often split into several amenity=hospital buildings under different names, e.g. UCLA's flagship building is tagged 'building=hospital' with no amenity tag, while its actual amenity=hospital-tagged sub-facility is 'Mattel Children's Hospital'). Verify against live Overpass data (or openstreetmap.org) before trusting a name, don't just use the hospital's common/marketing name. Insurance lists here are illustrative/plausible, not confirmed with the hospitals — always verify by calling.

hospital general de méxico.note: As Mexico's flagship public general hospital, it primarily serves patients without formal-sector employment insurance, largely through government safety-net health programs and subsidized care — treatment is low-cost or free relative to Mexico's private hospital sector. Reviews note the facility is chronically underfunded despite this critical public role. Foreign visitors are generally billed directly.

Private insurers listed here are mainly used for private hospitals, shorter waits for non-urgent elective care, or by visitors without SNS/EHIC entitlement, who are otherwise billed directly. Better known as Hospital Universitario La Paz, Madrid (its OSM-tagged official name is Ciudad Sanitaria La Paz).

hospital das clínicas.note: Brazil's SUS is a universal, tax-funded public system that provides free care to anyone in the country, including foreign visitors, at public hospitals like this one. Private insurers ("convênios"), usually employer-provided, are mainly used for private hospitals or to skip SUS wait times for non-urgent care. Full name is Hospital das Clínicas da Faculdade de Medicina da Universidade de São Paulo (HCFMUSP) — one of the largest hospital complexes in Latin America, run by the University of São Paulo.

北京协和医院.note: China's national basic medical insurance covers the large majority of the population but usually requires referral through a lower-tier facility first for full reimbursement at a top-tier hospital like this one, and still leaves a co-pay. Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH) is considered China's top-ranked hospital and has a dedicated international medical department for foreign patients and private-insurance/self-pay care. Google/OSM list its main East Campus separately as "北京协和医院东院".

policlinico umberto i.note: Italy's SSN is a tax-funded universal system, similar in structure to the UK's NHS — residents get free or nominal-copay ("ticket") care at public hospitals like this one. Private insurance is mainly used for private clinics or to skip public wait times for non-urgent care. Policlinico Umberto I, opened in 1903 and affiliated with Sapienza University of Rome, is one of the largest hospital complexes in Europe.

insurances: Free/means-tested at public hospitals under South Africa's public health system — no private insurance needed
Travel/international insurance for other visitors — verify directly
chris hani baragwanath hospital.note: South Africa has a two-tier system: public hospitals like this one are government-funded and charge low, means-tested fees (or nothing) directly, with no private-insurance billing involved, but face chronic underfunding and overcrowding. Private medical schemes (Discovery, Bonitas, etc.) are used almost exclusively at separate private hospital groups (Netcare, Life Healthcare, Mediclinic), not at public academic hospitals. Chris Hani Baragwanath, in Soweto, Johannesburg, is one of the largest hospitals in the world by bed count.

hospital de pediatría \"profesor doctor.note: Hospital Garrahan is a fully public, national-government-funded pediatric hospital — treatment is free for all children regardless of insurance status or nationality, reflecting Argentina's broader public-hospital system that provides free care to anyone in the country. Private "obras sociales" (union/employer health funds) and "prepagas" (private prepaid plans like OSDE and Swiss Medical) are Argentina's main insurance types generally, but are mainly used for private clinics rather than this hospital. Widely regarded as one of Latin America's leading pediatric hospitals.

uniwersyteckie centrum kliniczne wum.note: Poland's NFZ is a mandatory, payroll-funded national health insurance system — residents get free or low-cost care at public hospitals like this one, though non-urgent specialist care can involve long waits. Private insurers/subscription clinics (LuxMed, Medicover) are common as supplemental coverage for faster access, especially through employers. This is the Medical University of Warsaw's main clinical hospital on Banacha street — Google Maps lists it under a mix of current and older names ("Centralny Szpital Kliniczny WUM").

Travel/international insurance for foreign visitors — verify directly
مستشفي ابو الريش الجامعي للاطفال بالمنير.note: As a Cairo University-affiliated public children's hospital, care here is largely free and reliant on public funding and donations rather than insurance billing — several reviewers specifically encourage others to donate to support treatment for children whose families can't pay. Egypt's newer Universal Health Insurance law is being phased in region by region, alongside the older Health Insurance Organization for formal employees and a private insurance market for Egypt's separate private-hospital sector. Known in English as Abu El Reesh (or Abu Al-Rish) University Children's Hospital.

insurances: Bảo hiểm y tế / BHYT (Vietnam's national health insurance) — covers a large share of costs for insured residents, especially with a referral
Travel/international insurance for foreign visitors — verify directly
bệnh viện chợ rẫy.note: Vietnam's national BHYT health insurance covers the majority of the population and pays a large share of costs at public hospitals, but reimbursement is highest when patients go through a referral from a lower-tier facility first — going directly to a top-tier hospital like this one without one usually means a lower reimbursement rate. Private insurers are commonly used as supplemental coverage or by foreign residents. Cho Ray Hospital is Vietnam's largest and one of its most prestigious hospitals, drawing patients referred from across the southern half of the country.

insurances: SGK / Genel Sağlık Sigortası (Turkey's mandatory national health insurance) — covers most costs for insured residents
EU/EHIC reciprocal coverage for some European visitors
Travel/international insurance for other visitors — verify directly
i̇stanbul üniversitesi tıp fakültesi has.note: Turkey's SGK is a mandatory national health insurance system funded through payroll and government contributions, and public university hospitals like this one accept it directly. Private complementary insurance is mainly used for private hospitals or to reduce SGK co-pays. Also known as Çapa Hospital, this is one of two hospitals (along with the separately administered Cerrahpaşa Hospital) that trace back to Istanbul University's medical faculty, and the two are still sometimes confused with each other.

insurances: Regional tax-funded public healthcare (Sweden's universal system) — low fixed patient fees with an annual high-cost cap (högkostnadsskydd)
EU/EHIC reciprocal coverage for many European visitors
Travel/international insurance for other visitors — verify directly
karolinska universitetssjukhuset.note: Sweden's healthcare is funded through regional taxation, and residents pay only a small fixed fee per visit, capped annually — there's no US-style in-network/out-of-network split, and private insurance is uncommon for a hospital like this one, used mostly to skip queues for non-urgent private care. Karolinska University Hospital is one of Europe's largest and most research-intensive hospitals, closely tied to the Karolinska Institute, which awards the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

insurances: PhilHealth (Philippines' national health insurance) — covers a portion of costs, more for indigent/sponsored members
Free or heavily subsidized "service" (non-paying) wards for indigent patients, separate from paying wards
Travel/international insurance for foreign visitors — verify directly
philippine general hospital.note: PhilHealth is the Philippines' mandatory national insurance program, but it typically covers only part of a hospital bill, especially at private facilities. Philippine General Hospital is a public, government-subsidized hospital known for being far cheaper than private alternatives, with separate free "service" wards for indigent patients alongside paying wards — private HMOs (Maxicare, Medicard, etc.) are mainly used at private hospitals instead. Run by the University of the Philippines Manila, it's the country's largest public tertiary hospital.

insurances: EPS under Colombia's SGSSS (mandatory national health system) — Compensar
Travel/international insurance for foreign visitors — verify directly
clínica san ignacio.note: Colombia's SGSSS requires everyone to be enrolled in an EPS (health-plan administrator), either through the contributory regime (formal employment) or the subsidized regime (low-income residents), which then contracts with hospitals like this one for care. "Medicina prepagada" (private prepaid plans) exist on top of this for faster access or upgraded private rooms. Hospital Universitario San Ignacio is run by the Pontificia Universidad Javeriana and is one of Colombia's top-ranked teaching hospitals, though recent reviews describe significant strain on its emergency department.

lenox health greenwich village.note: This is Northwell Health's free-standing emergency department for Greenwich Village — it treats emergencies but does not admit inpatients overnight; more complex cases are transferred to Lenox Hill Hospital uptown.

nyu langone outpatient surgery center.note: An outpatient surgical center rather than a full hospital — used for same-day procedures like the trigger-finger release and minor orthopedic surgeries reviewers describe, not overnight stays or emergencies.

Eligibility and copays depend on the veteran's assigned VA priority group and service-connected disability rating.

It serves a very high volume of patients, including uninsured and low-income residents through LA County's own coverage programs.

white memorial medical center.note: Now operating as Adventist Health White Memorial after a rebrand — Google and other listings may show the newer name.

good samaritan hospital.note: Operates as PIH Health Good Samaritan Hospital — Google and other listings may show the newer name.

usc norris cancer hospital.note: A specialized cancer hospital, part of Keck Medicine of USC — typically used for oncology care, often alongside or following treatment at Keck Hospital of USC next door.

california hospital medical center.note: Operates as Dignity Health - California Hospital Medical Center — Google and other listings may show the fuller name.

gateways hospital.note: A psychiatric hospital and mental health treatment center (Gateways Hospital and Mental Health Center) — offers inpatient and residential mental health care, not general/emergency medicine.

insurances: Most major commercial plans (verify directly — long-term acute care coverage rules differ from general hospitals)
barlow respiratory hospital.note: A specialized long-term acute care hospital for patients needing ventilator support and weaning, tracheostomy care, and complex respiratory rehabilitation — not a general ER or short-stay hospital. Patients are typically transferred here from another hospital rather than arriving directly.

insurances: Kaiser Permanente health plans only — this facility generally does not accept other insurance
kaiser foundation hospital mental health.note: A Kaiser Permanente inpatient psychiatric and mental health facility. As with most Kaiser Permanente facilities, care here is normally restricted to patients enrolled in a Kaiser Permanente health plan, unlike most other hospitals in this app which accept a range of insurers.

insurances: Free or low-cost regardless of insurance status — a nonprofit community health clinic serving low-income and homeless residents
joshua house health center.note: Despite being tagged as a hospital in OpenStreetMap, this is a primary-care community health clinic (run by LA Christian Health Centers) in Skid Row, not a full hospital with emergency or inpatient care — it offers medical, dental, and pharmacy services on a free or sliding-scale basis.
